51601302.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to biotinylated KRAS G12D mutant (unknown origin) incubated for 120 mins by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: Biotinylated KRAS proteins (1-185, WT and G12D) were purchased from Amid Biosciences. For GDP loading, KRAS protein solution was mixed with 2x GDP buffer (40 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0), 200 mM NaCl, 30 mM DTT, 100 mM EDTA (pH 8.0) and 30 mM MgCl2) at the ratio of 1:1, followed by incubation at room temperature for 120 min. Reaction was quenched by the addition of 10% (v/v) of 1 M MgCl2. The final sample was freeze down with liquid nitrogen and stored at −80 °C until use. Binding kinetic assay was carried out on a Biacore 8 K+ (Cytiva) using biotin CAPTURE kit (Cytiva). Analysis temperature and sample compartment were set to 30 °C and 10 °C, respectively. HBS (10 mM HEPES-NaOH, 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.4) containing 1 mM DTT, 10 mM MgCl2, 10 μM GDP, 0.01% Tween 20 and 4% DMSO was used as running buffer. For the immobilization of GDP-bound form of biotinylated KRAS protein, Biotin CAPTURE reagent was injected into flow cell 1 and 2 followed by the injection of KRAS protein solution into flow cell 2. Immobilization levels of KRAS protein were about 250 RU. Interaction analysis was performed by a single-cycle kinetics of 100 μL/min. Test compound solutions of different five concentration were sequentially injected into flow cell 1 and 2 for 75 sec five times, followed by 3500 sec dissociation phase. Study data was analyzed using the Biacore Insight Evaluation software (Cytiva). The resulting sensorgrams were double-re-evaluated, DMSO-calibrated, and fitted by using a 1:1 binding model to determine parameters such as ka, kd and KD.

assay_conditions.running_buffer_composition: HBS (10 mM HEPES-NaOH, 150 mM NaCl, pH 7.4) containing 1 mM DTT, 10 mM MgCl2, 10 μM GDP, 0.01% Tween 20 and 4% DMSO

data_analysis.reference_description: Flow cell 1 (biotin CAPTURE reagent only, no KRAS protein)
